Query Azure MySQL as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__mysql.R
oauth_db_azure_mysql.Rd

Read Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server data with each visitor's Microsoft account and database permissions. The helper opens a MariaDB Connector/ODBC connection for DBI or dbplyr queries.

Usage

oauth_db_azure_mysql(
  authorization,
  server,
  database,
  user,
  driver,
  ...,
  port = 3306L,
  ssl_ca = NULL,
  target = "mysql",
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

server

One MySQL server hostname, usually ending in .mysql.database.azure.com.

database

Default database name.

user

Entra user or group name created in MySQL, or a reactive function returning that name. The server checks the identity mapping.

driver

Registered MariaDB Connector/ODBC driver name. Some driver managers also accept a library path. Use MariaDB Connector/ODBC 3.1 or later. MySQL Connector/ODBC uses different options and is not supported by this helper.

...

Result and timeout options: timeout, timezone, timezone_out, bigint, encoding, name_encoding, interruptible, or FORWARDONLY.

port

TCP port, default 3306.

ssl_ca

PEM CA certificate bundle path, or NULL to use the driver's trust configuration. Supply the bundle recommended for your Azure server.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A reactive function, usually named con. Call connection <- con() inside a render or reactive expression, then pass the connection to DBI. Before sign-in, the function waits quietly.

Details

Install odbc and MariaDB Connector/ODBC. Configure Azure MySQL for Entra authentication and create users or groups with the required database privileges. Use oauth_db_microsoft_client() with services = "mysql".

The helper sends the visitor's access token as the password through mysql_clear_password, with TLS certificate and hostname verification. MariaDB's client library supplies the cleartext plugin without a global environment setting. DSNs, option files, alternate credentials and automatic reconnection are disabled.

Create the helper inside server() and call con() before each query. The next access replaces the connection when its token or username changes. Ordinary token renewal does not rerun completed reactive queries. Sign-out, account changes and session end close the connection. If a query reports a broken connection, disconnect that native handle and call con() again. Failed queries are never replayed automatically.

See also

oauth_db_microsoft_client(). vignette("azure-mysql", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has sign-in setup and a complete app.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_azure_mysql(
  auth$connection,
  server = "example.mysql.database.azure.com",
  database = "reporting",
  user = "reporting-readers",
  driver = "MariaDB ODBC 3.2 Driver",
  ssl_ca = "path/to/azure-ca.pem"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT CURRENT_USER() AS database_user")
})
} # }
